newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: S.Korea PM asks lenders to support healthy firms.
newsitem.headline: S.Korea PM asks lenders to support healthy firms.

text.p: South Korean lenders should not be reluctant to extend loans to companies based on proper credit analysis despite jitters about rising corporate failures, Prime Minister Koh Kun said on Wednesday.

According to a summary of his remarks released in advance, Koh said he was concerned about financial institutions' reluctance to grant loans in the aftermath of a series of debt defaults and business failures.
He expressed his concern that some lenders were acting on rumours to either call in outstanding debts or deny new credits.
Koh was scheduled to make his remarks at noon to a gathering of presidents of commercial banks, heads of financial watchdog agencies and heads of non-bank financial associations.

In an apparent reference to the finance minister's warning last month that lenders who called in loans without good reason would be investigated, Koh said financial institutions which make sound decisions would not be punished.

Kang Kyong-shik last month told non-bank financial institutions the government would investigate lenders that moved too quickly to call in loans or those that made "unreasonable demands". -- Seoul Newsroom (822) 727 5644
